trail: Pitra Kripa, Vastu aur Hamara Jeevan: Ek Gehra Aur Pavitra Rahasya
text:
"Pitra sirf hamare purvaj nahi, woh hamari mitti, hamari DNA memory aur hamare aane wale kal ki aatma hain."
Zindagi mein jab bhi bina kisi wajah ke rukawatein aane lagein, property ya ghar lene mein baar-baar qanooni (legal) ya financial pareshaniyan ho, toh samajh lijiye ke kahin na kahin hamari jodon (roots) mein kuch healing ki zaroorat hai.
Yeh poori jaankari aapke ghar ki urja aur purvajon ke aashirwad ko ek sutra mein saja kar aapke jeevan ko saubhagyashali banane ke liye hai.

trail: 1. Pitra Kripa aur Property ka Sach (The Root Connection): -
text:
Karmic Clearance: Pitra Kripa koi darane wali shakti nahi hai, balki yeh ek aisi divya urja hai jo aapke raaste ke saare kaante saaf karti hai. Iske bina, kitni bhi mehnat kar lein, zameen ya makan kharidne mein rukawatein aati hi hain.
Sahi Santulan (The Equation): Jab aapka Purushartha (mehnat), grahon ki dasha, aur ghar ki Earth Element (Prithvi tatva) aapas mein milte hain, tabhi ek sthayi ghar ka sapna poora hota hai. Aur is poore safar mein Pitra Kripa woh catalytic force hai jo namumkin ko bhi mumkin bana deti hai.

trail: 2. Vastu aur Pitru Sthan — Sahi Disha ka Chunav: - Ghar ka har kona ek alag urja rakhta hai. Purvajon ki sthapna ya unke aashirwad ke liye sahi disha ka hona behad zaroori hai:
text:
Primary Pitra Zone (South-West / नैऋत्य कोण): Yeh sabse mukhya sthan hai. Yahan Rahu, Pitru aur Prithvi tatva ka vaas hota hai. Yeh ghar mein stability, heavy load aur inheritance (virasat) ko sambhalta hai.
Secondary Zone (South-South-West / SSW): Yeh विसर्जन (release) aur transition ka zone hai. Iska santulan purani urja ko mukt karke naye aashirwad lane mein madad karta hai.
Kahan KABHI Na Rakhein (Avoid Zones):
North-East (ईशान कोण): Yeh Devta aur jal ka sthan hai. Yahan pitron ki tasveerein rakhne se Dev Dosh lag sakta hai aur man ki shanti bhang hoti hai.
Mandir (Puja Room): Devta sattvic realm ke hain aur Pitru apne lok ke. Dono ki urja ko ek jagah milana uchit nahi hai.
Bedrooms, Kitchen, ya Bathroom ke paas: Yahan rakhne se purvajon ka anjane mein apmaan hota hai aur ghar mein financial crisis aane lagti hai.

trail: 3. Pitra Dosh Kya Hai? (Ek Karmic Rin): -
text:
Pitra Dosh koi shrap nahi hai, yeh sirf hamare karmic account aur genetic energy ka ek imbalance hai.
Lakshan (Symptoms): Bina kisi kaaran ke career mein bar-bar nakamyabi, shaadi ya santan hone mein deri, chronic health issues, aur ghar mein hamesha kalh ka mahol rehna.
Vastu Reflection: Agar aapke ghar ka South-West kona kata hua hai, wahan toilet hai ya underground water tank hai, toh samajh lijiye ki physical level par Pitra Dosh active ho chuka hai.

trail: 4. Shandar aur Asardaar Upay (Remedies for Healing): -
text:
Apne purvajon ki kripa paane aur dosh mukt hone ke liye ye kadam uthayein:
South-West ko Mazboot Karein: SW ki deewar ko bhari aur band rakhein. Apne purvajon ki tasveer South ya South-West ki deewar par is tarah lagayein ki unka chehra North ya East ki taraf ho. Tasveer hamesha saaf, glass-shielded aur akhand (bina tooti hui) honi chahiye. Zinda logon ke sath purvajon ki photo kabhi mix na karein.
Niyamit Seva: Har Amavasya ko Amavasya Tarpan karein. Kauve, stray dogs aur gay ko rozana khana khilayein — yeh hamare purvajon ke direct messengers maane jaate hain.
Pavitra Daan aur Jap: Mahamrityunjaya mantra ka jaap aur mandir ke paas Peepal ya Bargad ka ped lagana lineage ke karmic beban ko dhota hai.

trail: 5. Ghar ki Mahilaon ka Divya Achar-Sanhita (Code of Conduct): -
text:
Ghar ki naari is ghar ki Annapurna aur urja ka srot hai. Unke dwar ki gayi choti-choti baatein pure parivar ka bhagya badal sakti hain:
Kya Karein (Prashansaneeya Karya):
Rasoi (Annapurna Sthan) ko hamesha pavitra aur saaf rakhein. Khana hamesha shuddh vicharon aur muskurahat ke sath banayein, taaki woh poore parivar ki aatma ko poshit kare.
Shaam ke samay (Sandhya Kaal) mukhya dwar ke paas ya ek pavitra kone mein shuddh ghee ka diya jalayein aur ghar ki suraksha ki prarthna karein.
Kya Na Karein (Varjit Karya):
Raat ko sink mein gande aur jhoote bartan bilkul na chhodein. Yeh gahri nakaratmak urja aur financial tangi ko a आमंत्रित karta hai.
Sooraj dhalne ke turant baad ghar mein tezi se jhadu na lagayein aur na hi parivar mein kalesh ya gusse ka vatavaran banayein.

Parameter | Core Detail / Direction | Key Actionable Remedy
Primary Pitra Zone | South-West (SW) | Ghar ka yeh kona heavy rakhein; purvajon ki photo North/East face karke lagayein.
Forbidden Zones | North-East (NE) & South-East (SE) | Yahan heavy storage, mandir ya pitron ki tasveer rakhne se bachein.
Pitra Dosh Root | Karmic debt / Lineage imbalance | SW ke vastu dosh ko thik karein aur har Amavasya par daan-punya karein.
Property Success | Earth stability + Pitra Kripa | SW ko balance karke zameen/makan ki qanooni rukawaton ko door karein.
Mahilaon ka Niyam | Kitchen hygiene & evening prayer | Raat ko shrink mein jhoote bartan na chhoden, sandhya kaal mein diya jalayein.
Ek choti si baat: Purvaj naraaz nahi hote, woh sirf hamara dhyan apni taraf khinchte hain taaki hum apne jodon ko na bhoolein. Jab aap poore sammaan ke sath unhein unka sthan dete hain, toh poori kayanat aapke raste asaan kar deti hai.

1. Map the 16 zones — Orient the plan correctly and divide it into the selected 16-zone system.
2. Mark Brahmasthan — Identify the central area and avoid unnecessary heavy clutter.
3. Classify every object — Water, Fire/Heat, Electrical, Heavy, Movement, Disposal, Knowledge, Finance, Personal, Greenery, Security or Recreation.
4. Apply zone priority — Preferred → average/conditional → practical correction if unavoidable.
5. Check real-world safety — Gas, electricity, chemicals, sharp tools, medicines, water tanks, generators and vehicles require actual safety standards.
6. Check clutter — A favourable zone can still become poor if overcrowded, dirty, broken or inaccessible.
7. Check object separately — A room can be favourable while a small object inside it still needs its own functional placement.
8. Check height/weight — Heavy objects generally suit S/W/SW; light/open functions generally suit N/E/NE in this framework.
9. Check movement — Keys, luggage, vehicles, pets, laundry and tools fit movement-oriented zones.
10. Reassess — Review ventilation, daylight, access, ergonomics, noise, leakage, electrical load and cleanliness.

A Deep Architectural Study for Modern Society
Presented by Acharya Pankaj Kabiraj

To understand Vastu through the classical architectural tradition of Vishwakarma Prakash and to bring practical Vastu awareness to society—so that architecture is not treated merely as construction, but as a conscious relationship between land, direction, proportion, function, structure, environment and human life.

Vastu should not remain limited to a few traditional formulas, commercial remedies or fear-based predictions.
My objective is different.
I want to study Vishwakarma Prakash as an architectural knowledge system and explain its principles in simple, practical language.
The central idea is:
Every place where human activity begins deserves conscious planning.
That may be:
• A residential house
• A temple
• An office
• A school
• A hospital
• A shop
• A factory
• A public building
• A community centre
• A farm
• A garden
• A fort or institutional complex
• Or even an empty plot before construction begins
Therefore, Vastu awareness should begin before the building exists, not after problems appear.

Vishwakarma Prakash is a Sanskrit Vastu-Shastra text associated with the Vishwakarma architectural tradition.
The tradition presents Vishwakarma as the divine architect and teacher of architectural knowledge. Importantly, in scholarly presentation, it is better to say that the work is traditionally attributed to Vishwakarma, rather than treating the historical authorship as established fact.
The text itself preserves a transmission tradition in which architectural knowledge passes through earlier teachers and ultimately reaches Vishwakarma.
One traditional passage state:
इति प्रोक्तं वास्तुशास्त्रं पूर्वं गर्गाय धीमते।
गर्गात्पराशरः प्राप्तः तस्मात्प्राप्तो बृहद्रथः॥
बृहद्रथात् विश्वकर्मा प्राप्तवान् वास्तुशास्त्रकम्।
स विश्वकर्मा जगतीहिताय कथयत् पुनः॥

The Vastu knowledge was transmitted through a lineage of teachers—Garga, Parashara, Brihadratha and Vishwakarma—and Vishwakarma communicated the knowledge for the welfare of the world.
This is an important philosophical point.
Vastu is presented as knowledge for “Jagat-Hita”
Jagat-Hita: welfare of society / welfare of the world.
Therefore, my research objective is not to create fear about Vastu.
It is to bring architectural awareness to society.
The traditional lineage itself presents the knowledge as something intended for broader welfare.

ACHARYA PANKAJ KABIRAJ
VASTU AWARENESS THROUGH CLASSICAL ARCHITECTURAL KNOWLEDGE
“My objective is to bring the knowledge of Vastu closer to society—not through fear, superstition or commercial remedies, but through research, classical texts, architectural understanding and responsible modern interpretation.”

• No House Without Vastu Awareness.
• No Temple Without Vastu Awareness.
• No Office Without Vastu Awareness.
• No School Without Vastu Awareness.
• No Institution Without Vastu Awareness.
• No Plot Without Vastu Awareness.
Because the first step of good architecture is not construction.
The first step is awareness.

As a researcher, I believe we must distinguish three things:
1. What the Sanskrit text actually says — This should be quoted accurately.
2. What the traditional commentator or lineage interprets — This should be identified separately.
3. What we understand from it today — This is our modern interpretation.
This distinction is essential.
A responsible Vastu researcher should never present a modern interpretation as though it were the exact Sanskrit statement.

“Vastu is not about fear.
Vastu is about awareness.”
• Before buying land, understand the land.
• Before designing a building, understand its purpose.
• Before constructing, understand the site.
• Before occupying, understand the space.
• Before changing a building, understand its structure.
• And before quoting a Vastu rule, go back to the original text.
That is the spirit in which I want to study Vishwakarma Prakash.

trail: Vastu Is Not Only About the House

One of the most important lessons from studying classical Vastu texts is that Vastu cannot be reduced to:
• “Put this object in the North-East.”
• “Do not put this room here.”
• “Paint this colour.”
• “Buy this remedy.”
• “Move this furniture.”
Those are only fragments of a much larger subject.
The classical approach begins much earlier:
LAND → DIRECTION → MEASUREMENT → PROPORTION → FOUNDATION → STRUCTURE → SPACE → OPENINGS → FUNCTION → ENTRY → USE
This means that Vastu begins with the site itself.

trail: Every Problem in Life Is Caused by Vastu

“Every problem in life is caused by Vastu.”
That would be an oversimplification.
My message is:
Every building deserves thoughtful planning.
Vastu awareness should encourage people to examine:
• How is the land shaped?
• How is the building oriented?
• How are spaces connected?
• Are proportions appropriate?
• Is the structure safe?
• Is natural light available?
• Is ventilation adequate?
• Is drainage properly designed?
• Are the surroundings considered?
• Are trees and landscape respected?
• Does the building serve its intended users?
This is a much more responsible way to communicate Vastu.

trail: Vastu Purusha — Understanding the Architectural Idea
text:
The concept of Vastu Purusha is one of the most recognizable ideas in Vastu Shastra.
However, it should not be explained only as a mysterious figure lying on a plot.
At a deeper architectural level, the Vastu Purusha Mandala can be understood as a symbolic spatial framework through which the building site is organized.
It connects:
space + direction + order + proportion + sacred geometry + function.
This gives us an important principle:
A building should not be an accidental collection of rooms; it should have an organized spatial structure.
That is a principle modern architects can understand even without adopting every metaphysical interpretation.

A common misconception is that Vastu Shastra applies only to domestic interiors. However, classical treatises dedicate extensive frameworks to Durga-Vastu (fortress architecture) and urban master planning.
The tradition operates seamlessly across three distinct levels:
Micro Scale: Single-family homes & micro-interiors
Meso Scale: Institutional spaces, temples & civic gardens
Macro Scale: Fortified cities, royal complexes & regional layouts
Understanding Vastu as a multi-scale spatial methodology allows modern designers to appreciate its deep principles of proportion, zoning, and environmental balance at every level of planning.

I propose a simple principle for society:
“Do not wait for a problem to study the space.”
Study the space first.

trail: The Plot Is the Beginning of Architecture
The Plot Is the Beginning of Architecture
text:
The classical text gives considerable attention to the characteristics and forms of land.
This is extremely relevant today.
A plot is not simply:
“1000 square feet.”
Two plots having the same area may behave completely differently because of:
• shape
• orientation
• road position
• slope
• access
• surrounding construction
• drainage
• natural conditions
Therefore:
Area Alone Does Not Define a Good Site.
The quality and configuration of the site must also be examined.
This is one of the reasons I want to bring Vastu awareness to people before they purchase land, not only after construction.

trail: Site Analysis Comes Before Building Design
The First Principle: Start With the Land
text:
The first major architectural question should not be:
“Where should I put my kitchen?”
The first question should be:
“Is this land suitable for the proposed purpose?”
The first chapter of the available text deals with Bhumi-Lakshana—characteristics of land—and Bhumi-Phala, the traditional assessment of the consequences associated with different land conditions. It also includes excavation-related procedures.
This gives us a very important modern lesson:
Site Analysis Comes Before Building Design.
Before designing a building, we should understand:
• Plot shape
• Orientation
• Level differences
• Soil characteristics
• Drainage
• Access
• Surrounding roads
• Natural light
• Air movement
• Existing trees
• Water conditions
• Adjacent structures
• Environmental context
• Functional requirements
In modern architectural language, this is site analysis.
In classical Vastu language, the land itself is a subject of examination.

trail: Why Measurement Matters in Classical Vastu
A Classical Vastu Principle: Measurement Matters
text:
Another major subject in Vishwakarma Prakash is measurement.
The available contents specifically include:
• Ayavyaya-related calculations
• house classification
• door measurements
• pillar measurements
• house-hall arrangements.
This tells us something very important:
Traditional Vastu Was Concerned with Proportion.
Architecture is not simply about placing rooms in directions.
It is also about:
Length + Width + Height + Proportion + Openings + Structural elements.
A beautiful building can become uncomfortable if its proportions are poor.
Therefore, Vastu awareness should include the science of proportion and dimensional coordination.

This shows that residential Vastu was approached as a system of organized habitation.
• timing
• directional results
• Ayavyaya
• placement of deities/spatial functions
• house classifications
• door measurements
• pillar measurements
• house-hall arrangements.
The question was not merely:
“Which direction is lucky?”
The broader question was:
How should a dwelling be organized so that its spaces, proportions, openings and functions work together?
This is the kind of Vastu awareness that I want to communicate.

Vishwakarma Prakash is not limited to ordinary houses.
The available contents include Prasada-Vidhana, Prasada-Nirnaya, Pithika-Lakshana, and Mandapa-Lakshana.
This is extremely important for understanding Indian architectural heritage.
A temple is not simply a large building.
Its architecture integrates:
• sacred geometry
• axis
• proportion
• foundation
• platform
• entrance
• mandapa
• spatial hierarchy
• ritual movement
Therefore:
Vastu Is Also Sacred Architecture.

The final portion of the available 13-chapter text includes Raja-Griha-Nirnaya, or principles concerning royal residences, followed by the concluding section.
This again expands the scope of Vastu.
Architecture changes according to:
purpose + scale + hierarchy + function + users.
A palace cannot be planned exactly like a small residence.
Similarly today:
• A school is not a house.
• A hospital is not an office.
• A temple is not a shopping centre.
• A factory is not a residence.
Therefore:
Vastu Must Be Functional.

The text separately discusses Dvara-Mana, or door measurement, and later devotes a substantial section to Dvara-Lakshana, characteristics of doors.
This is significant.
A door is not merely an opening in a wall.
It controls:
• movement
• entry
• privacy
• circulation
• light
• ventilation
• visual connection
• symbolic transition
Therefore, when the classical tradition discusses doors, it is discussing an important part of architectural organization.

When we analyse a main entrance today, we should consider:
• approach
• orientation
• threshold
• circulation
• door proportion
• security
• natural light
• ventilation
• relationship to internal spaces
This creates a bridge between classical Vastu and contemporary architectural design.

The available contents also specifically identify Stambha-Pramana, or pillar measurement.
This is another reason why Vastu should not be reduced to decorative remedies.
Classical architectural thinking recognizes that:
Structure and proportion are connected.
The relationship between:
• foundation
• wall
• pillar
• door
• roof
• room
• overall proportion
creates the architectural character of a building.
Therefore, Vastu analysis should ideally work together with structural engineering and architectural planning, not against them.

A separate chapter deals with Vriksha-Chedana, or the traditional procedure concerning tree cutting.
This deserves careful modern interpretation.
It demonstrates that the traditional architectural system was aware that construction interacts with the natural environment.
Today, this principle can encourage us to ask:
• Can we preserve existing trees instead of removing them?
• Can the building be designed around valuable vegetation?
• Can landscape become part of architectural planning?
This transforms Vastu awareness from superstition into a broader conversation about responsible development.

The text also contains a section relating to Pushkara, gardens and mandapas.
This expands our understanding further.
Vastu is not only:
Building + Rooms
It also includes:
Building + Landscape + Water + Open Space.
This is highly relevant to modern sustainable architecture.
A good design must consider:
• landscape
• shade
• vegetation
• water
• open areas
• movement
• environmental comfort
Therefore, Vastu awareness can be connected with contemporary ideas of climate-responsive and ecological design, while keeping the historical distinctions clear.

An especially interesting section is Shalya-Jnana, literally dealing with the recognition of “shalya” or concealed disturbances/obstructions associated with a site.
For modern interpretation, we should be careful.
We should not automatically translate every traditional concept into a literal scientific claim.
Instead, the architectural question can be:
Are there hidden conditions on the site that may affect construction or habitation?
Today these may include:
• buried debris
• unstable soil
• old foundations
• drainage problems
• underground obstructions
• contaminated soil
• waterlogging
• abandoned structures
• construction waste
Thus, classical site-investigation ideas can inspire modern awareness, while actual engineering questions should be verified through appropriate professional testing.

One of the most important sections concerns Shanku-Shilanyasa and Shilanyasa, the processes associated with foundation and commencement of construction.
The foundation has both:
The structure must be properly established on the ground.

The beginning of construction is treated as an important transition between land and built form.
This gives us a powerful modern message:
The quality of a building begins before the first visible wall appears.
Therefore, Vastu awareness should start at:
Land selection → Site preparation → Foundation → Planning → Construction
rather than only at the interior stage.

trail: House Entry — Architecture Continues After Construction
text:
The tenth chapter deals with Griha-Pravesha, timing associated with entry, sleeping arrangements and related procedures.
This indicates that classical Vastu considered the building’s transition from:
constructed object → inhabited environment
to be important.
A building becomes meaningful when people actually occupy it.
Therefore, architecture should consider not only:
How do we build?
but also:
How will people live here?
